text: The Herbrand theorem says that a first-order formula φ is unsatisfiable iff:
choices: a finite propositional instantiation of φ (a Herbrand instance) is unsatisfiable
φ is a conjunction of literals
explanation: Herbrand's theorem: φ is unsatisfiable iff some finite set of ground instances of φ is propositionally unsatisfiable. This reduces first-order validity to propositional reasoning.
